chunks: 2705 - Abān narrated from Zurārah, who said:

I asked him about the muhrim: may he scratch his head or wash with water? He said: "He may scratch his head so long as he does not intentionally kill a small creature, and there is no harm in his washing with water and pouring it over his head so long as it is not matted. But if it is matted, then he should not pour water over his head except due to iḥtilām."

key_terms.احْتِلَامٍ: a state of ritual impurity resulting from a wet dream
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: a person in the state of ihram
key_terms.مُلَبِّدًا: having the hair matted or treated with a binding substance

ai.seo_question: Can a person in ihram scratch their head or pour water over it?
ai.summary: This hadith explains some rulings for the muhrim during ihram regarding scratching the head and using water. It permits scratching and washing so long as one does not intentionally kill a small creature and, in the case of a head treated or matted with a binding substance, water should not be poured over it except in the case of iḥtilām.
